deviations.what: SpreadsheetBenchAdapter.rollout() is replaced (subclass Exp895SkillOptAdapter in arms/skillopt/skillopt_exp895.py). It unpacks the skill document into a candidate dir and calls CommonRollout.evaluate(cand, ids, k=3, split=train|val). SkillOpt's codegen agent, executor and evaluator (skillopt/envs/spreadsheetbench/{rollout,codegen_agent,executor,evaluator}.py) are never called. Everything else is upstream code: scripts/train.py parse_args+load_config, ReflACTTrainer.train() (rollout -> minibatch reflect -> merge -> rank/select with the cosine edit budget -> apply -> selection gate, slow update and meta skill at epoch ends, sel_cache), SplitDataLoader, skillopt.gradient.reflect, the openai_compatible optimizer backend.
deviations.reason: Issue §7.3: 'Replace only rollout() with the common rollout. SkillOpt's own codegen agent and evaluator are not used.'

deviations.what: The skill document SkillOpt optimizes is ONE text = pack(task_template.md, skills/**/SKILL.md + scripts/*.py, prompt.md) with `=== FILE: <path> ===` marker lines (arms/skillopt/skillopt_pack.py). prompt.md is packed LAST so SkillOpt's tail-appending ops (`append` edits, the <!-- SLOW_UPDATE --> block) land in the system prompt. A document whose markers are damaged (text before the first marker, a missing prompt.md/task_template.md block, a duplicate / malformed / mid-line marker, a path outside the editable surfaces, an unbalanced protected block) is materialized as a stub whose task_template.md has no placeholders: the common adapter refuses it as error_kind=candidate before any model call, every trial scores 0 and the full evaluation is debited from R. The v2 seed round-trips byte-identically (self-check run by the launcher before every search).
deviations.reason: Issue §7.3: 'The artifact is ONE text, pack(prompt.md, task_template.md, skills/**) with === FILE: … === markers. A document with damaged markers scores 0 without a model call.'

deviations.what: `use_eval_feedback=True` (passed by the trainer to the train rollout) is ignored, and SkillOpt's _auto_verify_output (which prints expected-cell information) is not used. The reflect stage reads, per trial, predictions/<rid>/conversation.json = the agent's own transcript after the first user message (each message head+tail capped at 6,000 chars, whole conversation kept under 20,000 chars by dropping middle turns) plus one [POST-EXECUTION VERIFICATION] message = the common scorer's gold-safe feedback and any candidate-caused error; target_system_prompt.txt and target_user_prompt.txt = what the agent was sent (the user prompt includes answer_position, which the agent itself sees, as in every arm).
deviations.reason: Issue §7.3 'Feedback is gold-free. Ignore use_eval_feedback, since its gold-guided retry would leak.' The 20k cap is the same bound as GEPA's reflective records (§7.1); upstream sends untruncated trajectories, which at our 30-turn traces (P1 mean 117k prompt tokens/episode) would overflow GLM's context with minibatch_size=8.

deviations.what: Each task in a rollout call is scored k=3 times inside one CommonRollout.evaluate call, and returned to SkillOpt as 3 result rows `<id>`, `<id>__t1`, `<id>__t2` (each with its own predictions/<rid>/ dir). compute_score (and so the selection gate) takes the pooled mean over the rows. Trials still infra-errored after the common retries are dropped (missing, never 0). Upstream scores each item once. SkillOpt's slow-update / meta-skill longitudinal pairs (upstream build_comparison_pairs) are keyed by the task id, so each pair uses the `<id>` row (trial 0) and its trajectory; the pooled prev/curr hard scores it prints use all 3 rows. Upstream code, unchanged; a consequence of the row naming the issue prescribes.
deviations.reason: Issue §7.3 'k=3: one result row per trial (<id>, <id>__t1, <id>__t2); the gate takes the pooled mean'; §0.3 infra is missing, not 0.

deviations.what: R is enforced on the shared CommonRollout counter (BudgetStop before any evaluation that would overshoot). The port adds two look-ahead guards, raising BudgetStop: (a) a training step starts only if its train rollout (batch x 3) AND its selection eval (val x 3) both fit, so no train rollout is spent on a step whose candidate can never be scored; (b) a slow-update / meta-skill longitudinal pair (prev + curr rollout on 20 train items) starts only if both rollouts fit. BudgetStop propagates out of ReflACTTrainer.train(); the champion is SkillOpt's best_skill.md at that point (the best gate-accepted document on val; the seed if none was accepted). §5 optimizer-token cap (20M non-cache-read GLM tokens, from the gateway ledger) is checked at every rollout call and raises BudgetStop if exceeded.
deviations.reason: Issue §5 hard counter; §7 'Enforce R on the shared counter'; runaway guard.

deviations.what: When an optimizer call fails with an INFRA error (openai client: Request timed out / Connection error / HTTP 429 or 5xx, which includes the gateway's 502 after its own 8 attempts) after upstream's own retries, the wrapper waits 120 s and re-issues the whole upstream call, for up to 12 h per call; then upstream behaviour resumes (the exception propagates to upstream's handlers). Non-infra errors (e.g. HTTP 400) propagate immediately, as upstream.
deviations.reason: Upstream reflect/merge catch ANY exception and return None, so during a GLM outage a step becomes 'skip_no_patches' although its train rollout (batch x 3) was already debited from R. Seen live: GLM (Curve Bender) returned no 200 to any exp895 run from 2026-10-21T20:00:11Z on (all calls ReadTimeout at the gateway; runs/*/*/calls_glm.jsonl), which hit smoke_s0c (job 1923193, killed by exact id). Issue §0.3: infra errors are retried, never scored.
